summary: Citizens of the 96 countries and territories on Georgia's visa-free list (Government Resolution No. 255, as amended on 24 February 2026) — including the US, UK, EU, Ukraine, Turkey and Russia — can stay visa-free for a full year (Chinese citizens: 30 days, tourism only), while most other nationalities either qualify via a valid Schengen, US or UK visa or residence permit, or apply for a short-stay eVisa at evisa.gov.ge.

passportValidity.text: For a Georgian visa, including the e-Visa, the passport must stay valid for at least 3 months after the visa itself expires, have at least 2 blank pages, be undamaged and have been issued within the last 10 years. No Georgian source states a separate rule for visa-free visitors; the UK government advises a passport valid for the whole stay.

source.name: Georgia e-VISA Portal (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) — FAQ: document requirements and crossing the border

travelInsurance.text: Since 1 January 2026 every tourist entering Georgia must hold health and accident insurance covering the whole stay, with a sum insured of at least GEL 30,000, issued by a Georgian or foreign insurer and shown on paper or electronically in Georgian or English. Holders of diplomatic, official, service and special passports, accredited diplomatic staff and international drivers are exempt.

onwardTicket.text: A return or onward ticket is not on the official list of documents visa holders must carry at the border (passport, proof of the purpose of travel, accommodation, insurance and funds), and no rule is published for visa-free visitors.

source.name: Georgia e-VISA Portal (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) — FAQ: document requirements and crossing the border

proofOfFunds.text: Visa holders, including e-Visa holders, must carry documents proving sufficient financial means when crossing the border: a bank statement for the past three months, an employer's reference stating position and income, proof of owning property, or a sponsor's letter. No amount is published, and no official source states a funds check for visa-free visitors.

source.name: Georgia e-VISA Portal (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) — FAQ: document requirements and crossing the border

currencyLimits.text: You must declare to customs if you carry more than GEL 30,000 or its equivalent in another currency, according to Canada's travel advice, which links to the Revenue Service of Georgia. The Revenue Service's own page (rs.ge) says the same: cash, cheques and other securities over GEL 30,000 in total must be declared at the border, on entry and on exit.

source.name: Government of Canada — Georgia travel advice (money)

notes: The Revenue Service of Georgia allows travellers aged 18 or over to bring in duty-free, once per 30 days: 200 cigarettes (or 50 cigars, 50 cigarillos or 250 g of other tobacco), and 1 litre of drinks of 22% or more (or 2 litres under 22%) plus 4 litres of wine.

The UK FCDO says Georgia has a very strict anti-drugs policy that covers some medicines: non-prescription medicines containing codeine are illegal, and prescription medicine must travel with a doctor's prescription and in its original packaging. Check a specific medicine with the Revenue Service of Georgia or a Georgian embassy.

payments.text: The UK FCDO says prices may be quoted in US dollars or euros but goods and services must be paid for in lari, that travellers' cheques are rarely accepted, and that outside major towns you may not find ATMs or be able to use cards — take enough cash in lari for rural or remote areas.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says crime levels are low. It advises against all travel to the Russian-occupied regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia and all but essential travel next to their boundary lines, and says it cannot provide face-to-face support there.

idp.text: Georgia is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: Georgia is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Georgia yet.

tips.text: The UK FCDO says it is illegal under Georgian law to enter Georgia from Russia through South Ossetia or Abkhazia, with heavy fines or up to 4 years in prison. It advises against all travel to both regions and all but essential travel next to their boundary lines, which are generally unmarked.

The UK FCDO warns that roads outside city centres are often badly lit and poor, and that heavy rain, flooding and snow at higher altitudes can make travel difficult or impossible in remote areas. Make sure your vehicle is suitable for off-road driving and check weather conditions locally.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Georgia?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can enter Georgia visa-free and remain for a full year (365 days).

faq.question: How long can I really stay in Georgia visa-free?
faq.answer: A full year (365 days) for citizens of the countries on Georgia's visa-free list, including the US, UK, all EU states, Canada, Australia, Japan, Ukraine, Turkey and Russia. Chinese citizens, also on the list, may stay 30 days, for tourism only.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Georgia, and how much is it?
faq.answer: Yes, unless they hold a valid visa or residence permit from the US, UK, EU/Schengen or GCC states — in that case they enter visa-free for 90 days. Otherwise the short-stay eVisa at evisa.gov.ge costs USD 20 plus a 2% service fee and allows a 30-day stay within a 120-day window.

faq.question: Can I enter Georgia with a Schengen, US or UK visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Holders of a valid visa or residence permit issued by the US, UK, EU/Schengen states, GCC countries and several others can enter Georgia without a Georgian visa and stay for 90 days within any 180-day period.

faq.question: Can I visit Abkhazia or South Ossetia from Georgia?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to the Russian-occupied regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia and says it cannot provide face-to-face support there. It also says entering Georgia from Russia through either region is illegal under Georgian law, with heavy fines or up to 4 years in prison.
